name: A bad config pushed everywhere at once (global push)
description: Users go through an API gateway and a load balancer to 8 API servers. At 20 s the scenario deploys a bad config: the new version fails 60% of its requests, and it goes to every gateway and server at once (like Cloudflare's WAF rule in 2019 and its config file push in 2025). The whole site fails together until the end. Try this: in the scenario, set "Deploy a new version" to 4 waves, 10 s of watching per wave, and turn on "Automatic rollback threshold" at 5%. The first wave updates only a quarter of the machines, and the check rolls it back when it sees failures: only a small share of the requests in those first 10 s are hit (a small blast radius).
